ENDO01A|ENDO-11.src: Endotext Myxedema coma; DocT key (endo01a_review 22 Nov 2026)

fields.a:
- Cytokines, cortisol and fasting cut type 1 deiodinase (less T4 to T3) and raise type 3 (type 2 changes inconsistent) (more reverse T3), so T3 falls first.
- Hypothalamic TRH falls, so TSH is normal or low: an acquired, transient CENTRAL hypothyroidism (dopamine and steroids suppress TSH further).
- Low T3 alone = mild illness; low T4 with low TSH = severe (total T4 <4 microgram/dL carries up to about 50% mortality).
- In recovery TSH can rise transiently above normal (usually below 20 mIU/L) - this is not primary hypothyroidism.
- Do not screen TFTs or give thyroxine: treat the illness, feed the patient, recheck 4-6 weeks after recovery; treat only clear primary disease (TSH >20 with low free T4).

fields.a:
- Steroid-responsive encephalopathy with autoimmune thyroiditis: high anti-TPO, at ANY thyroid status (most reported cases subclinical or overt hypothyroid; older keys: usually euthyroid).
- Subacute confusion, seizures, myoclonus, stroke-like episodes, headache or visual change.
- CSF protein high, EEG diffusely slow, MRI often non-specific; a diagnosis of exclusion.
- High-dose steroids (methylprednisolone 1 g/day for 3-7 days, then taper) - the response is the confirmation.
- IVIG or plasma exchange if refractory.

fields.a:
- Paroxysmal headache, palpitations and sweating with episodic severe hypertension; crises are triggered by surgery, tumour handling, steroids, metoclopramide, beta-blockers and contrast. In pregnancy the episodic pattern with normal labs separates it from pre-eclampsia.
- Confirm with plasma free (fractionated) metanephrines, sensitivity 96-100% - COMT converts catecholamines continuously, so they stay high between bursts; 24-h urine metanephrines are the alternative.
- Image only after biochemistry (>3-4x upper limit is near-diagnostic); MRI in pregnancy (no MIBG or CT). In pregnancy (Bancos 2021, 249 pregnancies) maternal death or severe complication about 8% and fetal death about 9%, far higher if unrecognised (older keys: 40-50% mortality; crises at labour or anaesthesia), so remove the tumour laparoscopically in the second trimester or at caesarean section.
- Alpha-blockade FIRST: phenoxybenzamine or doxazosin for 7-14 days (ES 2014) with liberal salt and fluid; IV phentolamine 1-5 mg (or nitroprusside, nicardipine, clevidipine) for a crisis.
- Beta-blocker only AFTER alpha-blockade, and never labetalol first (beta:alpha about 7:1 leaves alpha unopposed). After removal expect hypotension and hypoglycaemia.

fields.a:
- Mediators (serotonin, histamine, bradykinin, prostaglandins) must reach the systemic circulation - usually only after liver metastases, because the liver inactivates gut-derived amines.
- Exception: bronchial, ovarian and retroperitoneal primaries drain outside the portal system, so they cause the syndrome WITHOUT metastases.
- Features: flushing, diarrhoea, bronchospasm, right-sided valve fibrosis (tricuspid regurgitation, pulmonary stenosis).
- Crisis (anaesthesia, tumour handling): octreotide IV bolus then infusion (NANETS 2017: infusions of 100-500 microgram/h are common practice); routine preventive octreotide is unproven. Older keys: 50-100 microgram bolus, 50-100 microgram/h.
- Avoid catecholamines and histamine releasers; use vasopressin or phenylephrine for hypotension.
